findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer bucket on the cook line measure 0ppm quaternary ammonia. The PIC was informed and replaced the bucket. There were multiple rags stored in the same small bucket. Too many rags in the same bucket can cause the concentration of the chemical to rapidly decrease. Inspector recommends reducing the number of rags in the bucket or increasing the size of the bucket to prevent this issue from occurring in the future.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the sealant between the counter to the right of the dish machine and the wall to be damaged. The PIC was informed and replaced the sealant during the inspection. This violation is now corrected on site.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed cook line to be in use with no sanitizer bucket prepared. PIC was informed that a sanitizer must be in use at all times during food preparation. A sanitizer bucket was created while on site and measured 100ppm chlorine. Violation is considered corrected on site.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed bare wood used as storage in the ware-washing area. PIC was informed that wood is absorbent and therefore not properly cleanable. Ensure facility is constructed with smooth, easily cleanable materials to prevent the accumulation of soil and bacteria.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed food handler’s certification for some employees to be absent or expired. PIC was informed that all employees who handle food, drinks, or ice need to have a valid food handler’s certificate within 30 days of hire. Ensure certificates are printed and readily available at next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed no paper towels available for use at bar hand washing sink. Paper towels were provided during inspection. 

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed ice cube tray stored on top of ice in bar ice bin. Ice cube tray was moved during inspection. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed knives on knife storage strip on cook line to be soiled with food debris. Knives were placed at dish area to be cleaned and sanitized during inspection. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Observed unlabeled spray bottle of liquid at bar. Spray bottle was labeled during inspection. 

7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Observed no sanitizer solution available for use in kitchen during food preparation. Sanitizer bucket was made and tested at 200 ppm quaternary ammonia. 

4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.
